description:
The Black Inc ZERO Track Disc is a revolutionary new wheel, developed in collaboration with the Australian Cycling Team and raced at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

Designed to maximise stiffness and aerodynamic efficiency, the ZERO Track introduces buttressed internal flange technology, creating internal shear walls between wheel faces that allow for reduced stiffness plies and an optimised carbon layup. The result is a disc wheel with incredible rigidity, lower weight, and world-class aero performance.

Wind tunnel tested extensively with AusCycling, the ZERO Track is optimised around 23mm tyres, ensuring the smoothest possible integration and lowest CdA. Its high-polished TexTreme carbon finish is not cosmetic — it’s the most aerodynamic surface identified during testing, proving that every design choice serves a performance purpose.

With both front and rear versions available, and a unique 40mm OLD hub option for modern pursuit forks, the ZERO Track is a true Olympic-grade wheel, now available to competitive riders worldwide.

Key Features at a Glance

Olympic Proven – raced by the Australian Cycling Team at Paris 2024

Optimised for 23mm tyres – best aero integration and CdA values

Buttressed Internal Flanges – unique shear wall structure for maximum stiffness and reduced layup weight

TexTreme Spread Tow Carbon – high-polished finish proven to be the most aerodynamic in wind tunnel testing

Available in front and rear versions – complete disc wheel solution

Hub options: Standard 100mm OLD or 40mm OLD pursuit fork spec (front)

Weight: ~1,100g rear / 1,000g front (approx., varies by spec)

Tubular only

Aerodynamics & CdA Efficiency

The ZERO Track disc has been optimised through wind tunnel testing with the Australian national team:

Optimised for 23mm tubulars → delivers the cleanest rim/tyre airflow transition.

High-polish TexTreme finish → proven more aerodynamic than cosmetic paint or clearcoat.

Front + Rear Disc Setup → provides the lowest total CdA (~0.230–0.245 m²), essential for pursuits and record attempts.

The Mavic Ellipse Track Wheelset is the world’s most popular training and entry-level racing wheelset for track cycling.

Designed in partnership with the UCI World Cycling Center, the Ellipse has become the benchmark for riders who want a reliable, stiff, and affordable wheelset without stepping up to carbon discs or specialist 3/4/5-spoke designs.

With aero-profiled 30mm Maxtal aluminium rims, QRM+ cartridge bearings, and bladed stainless-steel spokes, the Ellipse combines strength, stiffness, and smooth performance in a package that is perfectly suited to daily training, amateur racing, and velodrome hire fleets.

Key Features at a Glance

The world’s most popular alloy track wheelset – trusted by clubs and amateur riders worldwide

30mm Maxtal aluminium rims – lightweight, stiff, and durable

Stainless steel aero-bladed spokes – 20 front / 20 rear

QRM+ adjustable cartridge bearings – smooth, reliable, and serviceable

Double-sided fixed hub – ISO 1.375" x 24 tpi threading (supplied with 33mm x 1.0mm French lockring)

Why Choose the Mavic Ellipse?

Training Reliability: Designed for heavy daily use, with strong rims and robust hubs that stand up to years of track mileage.

Affordable Performance: High stiffness and responsive handling at a fraction of the price of carbon race wheels.

Beginner-Friendly: Clincher-only setup makes it simple to fit and maintain, perfect for new riders and clubs.

Event Suitability

The Ellipse is designed as a training and entry-level racing wheelset, making it ideal for:

Daily training (indoor and outdoor velodromes)

Beginner and amateur track racing

Club riders who want a dependable, affordable setup

For elite racing, riders upgrade to carbon discs (rear) paired with 3/4/5-spoke or disc fronts. For everything else, the Ellipse is the most reliable alloy option available.

Technology Explained

Maxtal Aluminium Rims: 30mm deep aero profile, lighter and stiffer than standard aluminium.

Bladed Spokes: Reduce drag slightly compared to round spokes, while improving stiffness.

QRM+ Bearings: Mavic’s serviceable, adjustable cartridge system ensures smoothness and long-term reliability.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is the Mavic Ellipse suitable for elite racing?
A: No. It is a training and entry-level racing wheelset. Professionals use carbon discs and spoked aero wheels for racing.

A: The Ellipse is durable, affordable, and widely available — making it the perfect balance of quality and price for training and club racing.

Q: What tyres can I use?
A: The Ellipse is clincher-only, compatible with 23–28mm track or road clincher tyres.

A: Yes. The aluminium construction makes it tough enough for rougher outdoor tracks as well as indoor boards.

description:
The Mavic iO is one of the most legendary wheels in the history of track cycling. First launched for the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, it quickly became the international reference for front wheels, winning over 80% of all Olympic and World Championship medals across two decades.

Updated for the Tokyo Olympic cycle, the latest iO features a wider rim profile, thinner truncated NACA-profiled spokes, and improved aerodynamics, delivering an average 25-watt saving compared to earlier models.

While Corima and Princeton’s

3 spoke wheels are now the most common choice among professionals, the Mavic iO remains an outstanding wheel for riders who want unmatched stiffness, proven heritage, and world-class performance.

Key Features at a Glance

Five-spoke carbon front wheel – iconic design, legendary Olympic pedigree

Aerodynamic lenticular body – reduces drag and improves efficiency

Truncated NACA-profile spokes – slimmer, more aero, and stiffer than previous models

QRM+ adjustable cartridge bearings – smooth, durable, and serviceable

Tubular only – optimised for 22–23mm professional track tubulars

Weight: 750g

Warranty: 2 years standard, lifetime with Mavic Care (registration required)

Includes: Crash replacement eligibility via Mavic Care

Aerodynamics & CdA

The iO’s five aero-profiled carbon spokes and lenticular body were revolutionary when introduced, providing significant CdA reductions compared to traditional spoked wheels.

Approximate CdA contribution (front wheel only):

3 Spoke: ~0.012–0.015 m² (best)

4 Spoke:

~0.015–0.018 m² (very good)

5 Spoke (Mavic iO):

~0.018–0.022 m² (higher drag, but stiffer and more stable)

While not the lowest-CdA front wheel by today’s standards, the iO’s extreme stiffness and predictable handling continue to make it attractive to powerful sprinters and riders who prefer its firm ride feel.

Why Choose the Mavic iO?

Proven Legacy: The most successful front wheel in track history, with decades of Olympic dominance.

Unmatched Stiffness: Its five-spoke design is incredibly rigid, ideal for powerful sprinters.

Heritage & Recognition: The iO remains an iconic piece of equipment, instantly recognisable on the track.

Updated Aero Design: Slimmer, more aerodynamic spokes with a truncated NACA profile.

Event Suitability

The iO is best paired with a rear disc wheel and is suitable for:

Sprint & Keirin – stiffness and stability for powerful accelerations

Points, Madison, Scratch, Elimination – stable handling in bunch races

Many elite sprinters still value the iO’s stiffness and planted front-end feel, even if its CdA is higher than modern 3- and 4-spoke wheels.

Technology Explained

Five Spoke Carbon Design: Maximises stiffness and stability under extreme torque.

Truncated NACA Spokes: Aerodynamic profiles based on aerospace engineering, slimmer than previous iO generations.

Lenticular Disc Body: Reduces turbulence and improves airflow across the wheel.

QRM+ Bearings: Fully adjustable cartridge bearings for long-term smoothness and serviceability.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is the iO still used by professionals today?
A: Less than before, as most pros now prefer 3- or 4-spokes for lower CdA. However, some sprinters and national teams still choose the iO for its stiffness.

Q: Why is the iO historically important?
A: It won over 80% of all Olympic and World Championship medals between 1996 and 2016, making it the most successful front wheel in track cycling history.

Q: What tyres should I use?
A: 22–23mm tubulars are the professional standard for integration with the iO’s rim profile.

Q: Is the iO better for sprinters or endurance riders?
A: It is particularly suited to sprinters, who benefit most from its extreme stiffness and stability.
